targets.review_note: For a proposed separation, each rooted subtree keeps a maximum-cardinality packing and maximizes its nearest selected distance among ties. Merge child packings in increasing nearest distance: when the closest two conflict, discard the closer selected vertex. Any other selected vertex from that same child is farther than the retained closest vertex by the within-child separation invariant, so no extra child state is needed. Once the nearest remaining vertex is far enough, add the current root. The resulting maximum count is monotone in the proposed distance, enabling integer binary search.

targets.review_note: For a fixed purchase order, collecting all required token pairs first is feasible, so the number of collection turns is the maximum of total red and blue expenditures. Track discounts instead of potentially huge costs: each purchased card saves at most the number of earlier same-color cards. For each subset and exact red discount keep the largest blue discount, since smaller blue discounts at the same state are dominated. Transitions depend only on the subset color counts and next card, and the final objective adds n purchase turns. Thus the DP covers every order without restricting cost magnitudes.
